end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from farm to plate.
Identified local food as travelling less distance than food from far away.
Compared examples including Shimla apples and Delhi spinach using distance and fuel.
Explained that longer journeys can require refrigeration, packing, more fuel and more pollution.
Teach-back was not passed; unaided answers were correct in 4 of 8 attempts.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles, identifying where foods come from, and comparing transport distance, fuel, pollution, freshness, refrigeration and packing. They used the farm-to-plate idea and correctly chose the 80 km farm because a shorter journey uses less fuel. There was a repeated-question mix-up about what to include for food travelling far; they later added packing alongside refrigeration and pollution (correctAfterLastSeen: true). At home, compare two foods in the kitchen and say which travelled farther and why that could affect fuel, pollution or freshness.
